blocks.text: INNNEWS - amidst many national issues that remain public concern, starting with economic inequality, corruption practices, questionable law enforcement, to various policies that reap the critics of society, the presence of intellectual organizations such as PIKI should not only function as a government partner, but also as a moral voice keeper.

As an organization that amasses Christian intellect, MIKI has the ethical responsibility to voice truth and justice, including when the vote does not match the political interests of the ruler. The intellectual and Christian values teach the truth, not the power. Therefore, the primary measure of organization's success is not his approach to the government, but his courage to convey constructive criticism for the benefit of the people and the nation.

The appointment of an active official as a general chairman certainly raises a public question about the ability of organizations to keep his attitude independent. In a situation like this, PIKI just needs to prove that she's not moving into an instrument of power legitimacy. MAN must remain able to voice a critical view of public policy that is judged not to side with the public.

The critics that appear are not critics against the private Maruarar Sirait. It has the same rights to lead a society organization. The question is how to make sure that PIKI doesn't lose its primary function as a moral force and an independent think tank. An intellectual organization should be able to criticize the government when policy is judged not to side with the people, including if that policy comes from the ministry led by its own general chairman.

These concerns are increasingly relevant when a number of statements from the new caretaker place PIKI as "strategic partner of the government" and organizations that want to influence state policy. Being a government partner certainly doesn't matter. However, partnership must not turn into a closeness that reduces critical power of the organization.

History shows that many organizations lose relevance when it's too late in power orbit. Internal critics are weakened, debate space is narrowed down, and organizations are busier to maintain a relationship with the elite than to fight for member aspirations. This condition needs to be anticipated from the start by PIKI.

Public belief in intellectual organizations is born of its consistency in defending the truth. When organizations prefer silence to the matters of the nation due to political closeness consideration, their intellectual and moral functions will lose their meaning. Instead, if the PIKI is able to show moral courage to speak objectively and independently, then this organization will remain relevant as a respected power of thought, both by governments and vast communities.
